newsitem.title: USA: Watergate guard Willis recalls night of burglary.
newsitem.headline: Watergate guard Willis recalls night of burglary.

text.p: Frank Willis, the security guard who foiled the break-in at the Watergate complex 25 years ago Tuesday, said he planned to celebrate quietly at home smoking a rare cigar and perhaps enjoying a beer.
"I'll smoke me a cigar. I haven't had a cigar in a long time. Maybe have a cold one, you know," he told the Augusta Chronicle.

Willis, 49, was a 24-year-old guard coming off his break at the Watergate office and apartment complex June 17, 1972, when he noticed that a basement door had been taped open. He promptly phoned police, launching a cascade of events that led to a constitutional crisis and the eventual resignation of President Richard Nixon two years later.
Willis said his usual midnight-to-8-a.m. shift that day started "like a regular night." But it ended with his becoming a footnote in American history.
He now lives at his family home in North Augusta, Ga., doing odd jobs and caring for a stroke-ridden aunt.
